title: the sandals
hook: two brothers argue on a mountain, each trying to give the other a kingdom

segments.voice: Yesterday: your line, he comes in love. Guha and Bharadvaja questioned Bharata; Rama never doubted him.

On Chitrakoot, two brothers have an inheritance fight that runs backward: each one is trying to give the kingdom away. Bharata reaches the hut, sees Rama in bark clothes with matted hair, and falls at his feet, unable to finish a sentence. Rama lifts him up, holds him, and asks the question Bharata has dreaded the whole road. Where is our father? Why have you left him to come here?
screen: `A FIGHT TO GIVE THINGS AWAY.` → `BHARATA AT RAMA'S FEET.` → `WHERE IS OUR FATHER?`

segments.voice: Bharata tells him. The king is dead, grieving for you. Rama falls like a cut tree. When he can stand, he goes down to the Mandakini with his brothers and Sita, and offers his father water and a ball of ingudi pulp, the forest food they've been living on. In Valmiki's telling, he says: what a person eats, their ancestors eat too. Then the arguing begins, and it goes on and on. Bharata pleads: come home, be king, I'll serve you. Counselors and priests plead. Rama's answer never changes. Our father gave his word to Kaikeyi and made a promise to me. Keeping his word is how I honor him now. Fourteen years in the forest is my part; ruling Ayodhya is yours. Bharata even threatens to sit fasting at the door of the hut until Rama gives in, and Rama gently tells him that isn't the way. Finally Bharata asks for one thing. He brings out a pair of sandals adorned with gold, and asks Rama to step into them, then give them to him. Rama does. Bharata bows to the sandals. For fourteen years, he says, these will rule. I'll live outside the city in bark and matted hair, waiting for you. And if you're not back the day after fourteen years end, I'll enter the fire. Neither brother wins the argument. Both keep their word.
screen: `WATER FOR A FATHER AT THE MANDAKINI.` · `COME HOME AND BE KING.` · `I KEEP MY FATHER'S WORD.` · `STEP INTO THESE SANDALS.` · then, large: `BOTH KEEP THEIR WORD.`

segments.voice: Bring to mind one object that keeps someone present for you while they're away, a photo, a ring, a cup they gave you, and picture its color and its weight. Notice how a small thing can carry a whole person, and let them be near while you breathe.
The sandals. Rama steps into a pair of gold-adorned sandals and gives them to Bharata, who will set them on the throne for fourteen years.
Your line: both keep their word. Neither brother wins, and neither breaks a promise. See you tomorrow.

howItsDone: Rama's sandals, the padukas, are honored in Hindu worship and art, and Ramlila performances stage the brothers' meeting at Chitrakoot.

fork.setup: you're Bharata. Rama won't come home, no matter what anyone says. what do you ask for?
options: his bow, as a sign of power.
his sandals, after he steps into them.
a written order making you king.
fork.reveal: he asks Rama to step into a pair of gold-adorned sandals, then carries them home to rule in Rama's name.

original.note: Sanskrit pādukā: a sandal or wooden shoe. Rama's pādukā are still honored in temples and homes.

trapdoor: what you thought: Bharata takes the sandals as a keepsake.
what it means: he takes them to place on the throne and rule in Rama's name.
what a scholar hears: Valmiki has Bharata ask Rama to step into the sandals first, so they carry his presence, and vow fire if Rama is late.

chat.says: Why would Bharata take Rama's sandals home instead of just taking the throne?
options: To rule in Rama's name, so both brothers could keep their word.
As a keepsake, since he feared he'd never see his brother again.
Because Rama ordered him to wear them as the new king of Ayodhya.
chat.meaning: Rama wouldn't break his father's word, so Bharata asked him to step into the sandals, and took them home to rule in Rama's name.

Mandakini.meaning: the river at Chitrakoot where Rama offers water to his father

ingudi.meaning: a forest tree; its fruit pulp was the exiles' food

Chitrakoot.meaning: the mountain where the exiles made their forest home

Kaikeyi.meaning: Bharata's mother, the queen who asked for the two boons

sources.ref: Valmiki Ramayana, Ayodhya Kanda 99–103 (the meeting; the news; the offering at the Mandakini)
Valmiki Ramayana, Ayodhya Kanda 104–112 (the pleas; Rama's refusal; the sandals)

notes: Jabali's argument and Rama's reply (Ayodhya 108–109) and Rama's long questions on kingship (Ayodhya 100) are left out for one idea; a Keeper may want them on a later day.
